questions.q: What does this lesson say is the least important part of the scoring step, at capstone scale?
options: The specific scoring logic itself — a threshold rule proves the pipeline end to end, and a trained model can swap in later without changing anything around it
Whether the pipeline runs in real time at all
The feature records computed in the previous lesson
Whether the alert reaches the fraud-review queue
questions.explain: What matters is that scoring consumes exactly one feature record and produces exactly one decision — the rule itself can be swapped later.

questions.q: Why is Activator described as a natural fit for turning a fraud flag into a real alert?
options: It's built to watch a continuous stream and fire an action once per qualifying event, exactly the shape needed for alerting on a flagged transaction
Activator can only be used with batch data
Activator requires a trained machine learning model to function
Activator replaces the need for a scoring rule entirely
questions.explain: Activator was introduced in Fabric as the mechanism for turning a streaming condition into a real action without hand-rolling the plumbing.

questions.q: Why doesn't at-least-once delivery, on its own, prevent duplicate fraud alerts?
options: At-least-once only guarantees an event is delivered one or more times — "exactly-once effect" has to be built on top of that guarantee, not assumed from it
At-least-once delivery guarantees zero duplicates by definition
Duplicate alerts are impossible in streaming systems
At-least-once delivery only applies to batch pipelines
questions.explain: If the platform redelivers an event after a transient failure, the same transaction can trigger scoring twice unless a safeguard is added.

questions.q: How does the MERGE-based alert write prevent a duplicate alert on event redelivery?
options: It's keyed on transaction_id, so a redelivered event matches the existing row and the insert becomes a no-op
It deletes the previous alert before inserting a new one
It uses a random key so duplicates are statistically unlikely
It relies on the streaming platform to filter duplicates automatically
questions.explain: This is the same targeted-upsert pattern used for SCD merges and Delta MERGE INTO — a keyed write makes redelivery harmless.

questions.q: Why does this lesson emphasize that idempotency was flagged back at Project 3's kickoff, before any scoring logic existed?
options: Because idempotency is a design requirement that has to shape the pipeline from the start, not something bolted on after alerts start duplicating
Because idempotency only matters for the ingestion step, not alerting
Because the kickoff lesson is unrelated to this one
Because scoring logic cannot be idempotent by definition
questions.explain: The requirement to never double-alert on the same transaction was called out as a first-class, non-functional requirement at kickoff.
